card.title: Understand the Hurt
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I saved you a front-row seat at my concert. Do you understand why it hurt?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you work might run late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I knew. I still looked at that empty seat before every song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You needed someone there who knew what this meant to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You'd heard me practise for months. Please tell me you understand why someone else couldn't fill it.

mechanism: A seeks acknowledgment that this particular person's absence hurt because they knew the work and significance of the concert.
confusable: Unlike only confirming an empty seat, A must explain why that action carried personal meaning.
comparison: D99-a ties unique knowledge to an unfillable seat; D99-b ties a dinner message after job loss to feeling reduced to service.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
